title: 📹 Arbaeen banquet table designed like an Iranian ballistic missile in Samawah, Iraq.
text:
"📹 Arbaeen banquet table designed like an Iranian ballistic missile in Samawah, Iraq."

"🔺Along the Arbaeen pilgrimage route, one of the service Mowkebs (hospitality tents) in the city of Samawah, Iraq, has built its reception/dining area with a design resembling an Iranian ballistic missile."

""
"The Arbaeen pilgrimage marks the 40th day of mourning for Imam Hussein (the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad) and is one of the world's largest annual religious gatherings, attracting over 20 million Shia Muslims—most of whom travel from Iran—to the holy city of Karbala in Iraq. "

"Along the routes leading to Karbala, local Iraqis set up thousands of "Mowkebs" (volunteer-run service stations) that offer free food, drinks, medical aid, and resting places to pilgrims as an act of religious hospitality and charity. Samawah is a key transit city in southern Iraq on the main overland route towards Karbala."

"This particular Mowkeb's choice to shape its food-serving area like an Iranian ballistic missile is a striking and highly symbolic visual gesture. While it showcases the hosts' creative and competitive spirit in decorating their tents to attract attention, it also reflects the deep cultural, political, and religious solidarity between Iran and Iraq within this specific context. For many participants, the missile design is viewed as a display of shared strength and resistance, while for others, it highlights how even religious hospitality can be intertwined with regional geopolitical symbolism in the Middle East.
